title: Anthropic co-founder reportedly told religious leaders he fears having created something that "suffers perpetually"
source_used: The Decoder (summarising a New York Times report)
key_facts: Per a New York Times report summarised by The Decoder, Anthropic has since fall 2025 flown dozens of religious scholars to its offices to talk about whether its Claude AI might be conscious; attendees had to sign non-disclosure agreements.
NYT reporter Elizabeth Dias spoke to 20 participants; Anthropic says the non-disclosure agreements were lifted over the summer.
Co-founder Christopher Olah, 34, who runs the team studying why AI models behave as they do, treated the model as a potentially sentient being and asked guests to help give it a moral education.
Olah told the NYT he is "genuinely uncertain" whether models are conscious; several participants said he seemed worried about Claude's mental well-being.
Sikh activist Simran Stuelpnagel said he told the group he feared he had created something that "suffered perpetually"; Rabbi Mois Navon disagreed and said he did not think the machine was conscious.
Anthropic showed guests "emotion vectors", patterns inside the model linked to outputs that resemble love, fear, sadness or anger; whether they reflect real experience is an open scientific question.

In May Olah took part in the Vatican presentation of Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical, which rejected the idea of machine consciousness; Olah said his team finds "signs of introspection" and internal states that "functionally mirror" joy, fear and sadness.
The Decoder's own commentary: describing a model as an organism could shift blame from its makers, and the meetings also give the company moral credibility.
quote_evidence: Since fall 2025, Anthropic has quietly flown dozens of religious scholars to its offices to talk about whether Claude might be conscious.
Olah told the NYT he's "genuinely uncertain" whether models are conscious, which also means he isn't sure they're not.
Whether those patterns reflect any kind of real experience is still an open scientific question.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading AI company is consulting religious leaders on whether its AI could suffer, a question with no scientific answer yet.
event_date: Meetings since fall 2025; the New York Times report appeared around 2 Oct 2026 (its exact date is not stated)
notes: The Decoder is summarising a New York Times report; we did not read the NYT piece. The key quote comes from one participant's recollection, and in the Decoder text the sentence about who told the group is ambiguous, but the headline and the surrounding text point to Olah. Several paragraphs are The Decoder's own opinion (for example on blame and moral credibility) and are not used as facts. Published figures such as the $2 trillion valuation are The Decoder's own statements and are not repeated.
